title: Two fixed stores can hide slow-path loss within a small absolute flow error
abstract: We test whether near-proportional seasonal flow excludes preferential loss of slow-path flow. For two parallel linear stores with equal recharge and fixed rates, an explicit routing model retains 78.4% of mean flow. With 5-day and 200-day drainage times, its annual-cycle flow ratio stays between 77.73% and 79.00%, while its day-3 to day-8 decline index rises from 0.2079 to 0.2316. The slow path loses a larger fraction. We prove an exact largest-frequency-error formula. With the same mean retention and endpoint indices, the absolute transfer error over all frequencies can approach zero as slow storage grows without bound and absolute impulse flow shrinks. A bound links endpoint error to event-flow amplitude. Thus exact seasonal exclusion does not imply a stable test at a fixed absolute tolerance without storage or signal limits. High-precision checks, independent state integration, proof, code and synthetic results are included. This is a model result, not a catchment fit or a physical explanation of Australian runoff loss. Equal recharge, linear parallel stores and separate periodic and impulse experiments limit field use.

display.caption: Synthetic two-store tests show a near-constant seasonal flow ratio, a larger normalized decline, and the storage cost of reducing absolute transfer error. This is not a field fit.

citations.reason: Uses scalar model anchors and extends its exact monotone-routing restriction to finite absolute tolerance.
